content:
This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday executive summaries work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical executive summaries tasks.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Measure before optimizing any executive summaries bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
2. Prefer explicit, readable executive summaries solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
3. Before starting executive summaries work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
4. Surface known limitations of a chosen executive summaries approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
5. Validate executive summaries outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
6. When multiple executive summaries strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
7. State assumptions about executive summaries explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
8. Prefer the simplest executive summaries approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
9. Check that executive summaries terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
10. Keep executive summaries changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic executive summaries advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Avoid mixing unrelated executive summaries concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not silently drop executive summaries edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid introducing new executive summaries abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these executive summaries guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
